title: Unified Multi-Provider SDK Patterns
summary: For intermediate developers, this module teaches a thin adapter over the native Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google APIs. Learners normalize provider response shapes, terminal states, tool requests, usage, and storage behavior without assuming that compatibility endpoints or model families share one wire contract. A deterministic Node.js 22 lab repairs one ordering defect in a final-response OpenAI Responses adapter.
objectives: Map Claude Messages, OpenAI Responses, Gemini generateContent, and Gemini Interactions responses onto one internal ModelResult contract.
Classify terminal state before exposing ordinary completion or executable tool calls.
Fail closed on unknown statuses, malformed envelopes, malformed content parts, and function calls without an actual call_id.
Distinguish deterministic fixture simulation from authenticated live integration testing.
Keep model identifiers, API surface, storage policy, and source provenance in configuration.

sections.title: Three providers, four native response shapes
paragraphs: A portable client starts by acknowledging that providers do not share one response schema. The Claude Messages API accepts a top-level `system` parameter and a `messages` array. It returns an assistant message whose `content` contains typed blocks such as `text` and `tool_use`. The application resends the history needed for a stateless multi-turn conversation. See Anthropic's [Create a Message](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages/create) documentation.

OpenAI recommends the Responses API over Chat Completions for new projects. A Response has a top-level status and an `output` array of typed Items. A `message` contains content items such as `output_text` or `refusal`, while a `function_call` is a separate output Item. Responses are stored by default unless the request uses `store: false`. See OpenAI's [Migrate to the Responses API](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses) guide.

Google documents two Gemini surfaces. `generateContent` returns `candidates[].content.parts[]` and a `finishReason`, where `STOP` represents a normal finish. The Interactions API returns an Interaction with a status such as `completed` or `requires_action` and steps such as `model_output` and `function_call`. Google recommends Interactions for new projects while describing `generateContent` as legacy but supported. See the [Gemini models](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models) and [Interactions API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions-overview) documentation.
The common abstraction belongs inside the application. It does not establish that the providers validate tools, represent refusals, store state, stream events, or report usage in the same way.
sections.callout: Normalize into an internal contract only after validating the native provider envelope.

code.label: Stable internal result contract

sections.title: Classify state before releasing a result
paragraphs: Terminal state controls what downstream code may do. Claude documents stop reasons including `end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `refusal`, `tool_use`, and `pause_turn`. OpenAI Responses uses `completed` or `incomplete`, with an incomplete reason that can be `max_output_tokens`. Gemini `generateContent` uses `finishReason`, while Gemini Interactions uses its top-level status.

Text does not prove completion. A final response snapshot can contain partial message text while its status remains incomplete or otherwise noncompleted. Preserve that text for diagnostics or an explicitly marked partial display, but do not label it complete.

A function-call-shaped item does not by itself authorize execution. In this lesson's final-response adapter, a call becomes executable only when the enclosing response is `completed`, the function-call item is structurally valid, and it has its own nonempty `call_id`, name, and arguments. An item's unrelated `id` must never be substituted for `call_id`. Incomplete, queued, in-progress, failed, cancelled, unknown, or malformed responses expose no executable tool calls.

Mappings must be total. Known values receive explicit outcomes. Unknown values become `other`. Malformed envelopes and parts also become `other` without throwing. The adapter retains the provider status or incomplete reason as `rawStop` and retains valid raw usage as `rawUsage`.

This lab adapts final response snapshots, not streaming events. A streaming dispatcher needs a separate state machine that accumulates deltas and waits for the provider's terminal event before authorizing a tool or declaring completion.

code.label: Provider-specific outcome sketches

sections.title: Worked example: incomplete text and a call-shaped item
paragraphs: The worked fixture has `status: "incomplete"`, `incomplete_details.reason: "max_output_tokens"`, partial text `Draft: inspect the`, and a structurally valid `function_call` item. The correct normalized result is `truncated`, with the partial text preserved and `toolCalls` empty.

The causal sequence is important. First, the envelope is a valid final-response snapshot. Second, its top-level status says generation is incomplete. Third, `max_output_tokens` supplies the established truncation mapping. The response therefore cannot authorize its call-shaped item, even though that item has a `call_id`, name, and arguments.

The deliberate starter defect checks for a ready function call before it handles the incomplete status. That leaks the call as `tool_request`. The focused repair moves incomplete classification before the function-call branch. Ordinary messages already require `status: "completed"`, so moving this one branch fixes the defect without weakening other validation.

The repaired result is `{ provider: "openai", surface: "responses", model: "fixture-model", outcome: "truncated", text: "Draft: inspect the", toolCalls: [], rawStop: "max_output_tokens" }`. The usage object is also retained.

sections.title: Compatibility endpoints do not create identical semantics
paragraphs: Anthropic and Google both document ways to use OpenAI-oriented client libraries with their services, but their compatibility behavior is provider-specific.

Anthropic documents that its OpenAI SDK compatibility layer ignores the strict tool flag and `response_format`, caps temperatures above 1 at 1, and hoists system messages. Anthropic presents that route primarily for testing and comparison rather than as the preferred long-term production interface. See [Anthropic OpenAI SDK compatibility](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/openai-sdk).

Google documents that its OpenAI compatibility route maps `reasoning_effort` to Gemini thinking settings and uses `extra_body` for Gemini-specific features. The cited Google material does not establish the same ignored-field behavior documented by Anthropic. See [Google OpenAI compatibility](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai).

A successful request proves only that the endpoint accepted that request. If an application depends on strict tool arguments, structured output, refusal detection, storage control, or a particular event sequence, test that guarantee on the exact provider, API surface, model, and SDK version used in deployment.
sections.callout: Never copy a limitation documented for one compatibility route onto another provider without a source and a contract test.

code.label: Guarantees are tests, not assumptions

sections.title: Configure model, surface, and storage policy explicitly
paragraphs: Keep the concrete model identifier outside adapter code. Record the provider, API surface, model identifier, storage policy, verification date, and authoritative source. Do not silently fall back to an unreviewed model.

Claude Messages relies on the application to resend conversation history. OpenAI Responses stores by default unless `store: false` is set. Gemini Interactions stores by default, and Google documents that `store=false` prevents chaining with `previous_interaction_id`. An adapter should translate an application retention policy into surface-specific controls or reject a combination it cannot honor.
An offline fixture cannot prove that a model is currently available to an account or region. That requires an authenticated live integration test against the configured route.

code.label: Route configuration with provenance

sections.title: Retry transport failures, not model outcomes
paragraphs: Refusal, truncation, pause, and a valid tool request are model or application outcomes. They are not generic transport failures and should not be retried blindly.

A retry policy needs a maximum attempt count, a total elapsed-time or budget limit, and cancellation propagation. Retrying a generation request can duplicate token charges. Retrying tool-result submission or another mutation can duplicate side effects.

Retry a mutation only when the exact provider operation documents an idempotency mechanism and the adapter reuses the same idempotency key. If that guarantee is absent or unknown, return an uncertain result for reconciliation instead of issuing a blind retry.

code.label: Bounded retry skeleton

sections.title: Transfer the adapter method, not the wire mapping
paragraphs: The adapter method applies beyond these three providers, but the concrete mappings do not. Meta Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, and Microsoft Phi can name model families or released artifacts rather than one hosted API.

A model can be served by a first-party runtime, a cloud endpoint, a third-party inference server, or a compatibility gateway. Those layers can expose different tool formats, stop fields, token accounting, streaming events, and persistence policies.

Begin transfer work with the official project material for the chosen artifact, such as [Meta llama-models](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models), [Qwen3](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3), [DeepSeek-V3](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3), [Mistral inference](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-inference), or [PhiCookBook](https://github.com/microsoft/PhiCookBook). Then consult the documentation for the actual serving runtime. Record model family, concrete identifier, runtime or service, and API surface separately.

sections.title: Fixture simulation and live integration answer different questions
paragraphs: The supplied lab is a deterministic fixture simulation. It makes no network call, needs no API key, and incurs no model charges. It tests local parsing, fail-closed behavior, call readiness, call-id handling, and outcome precedence.

A live integration test uses credentials and a native provider surface. It can establish that a configured account can reach a model and that observed responses satisfy a contract on the test date. It can also be billable, nondeterministic, region-dependent, and affected by provider changes.

Keep live tests in a separately named target. Record provider, surface, model, storage setting, SDK version, date, budget, cancellation behavior, and observed result. No live provider call or lab command was executed while drafting this artifact.

sections.title: Repair lab: do not execute calls from an incomplete response
paragraphs: Run `node training/developer-and-practitioner-ai/provider-sdk-patterns/lab/verify.mjs` from the repository root. The starter performs 17 immutable checks. Exactly one check fails: the incomplete fixture is incorrectly classified as `tool_request`. The other 16 checks pass.

Edit only `adapter.mjs`. Move the incomplete-status branch before the completed-response tool branch. Preserve text extraction, raw diagnostics, completed-message classification, refusal classification, function-call validation, exact `call_id` use, noncompleted call suppression, and malformed-input handling.

After the repair, all 17 checks pass. The verifier covers `in_progress`, `queued`, `failed`, and `cancelled` responses containing function calls. Each maps to `other` and exposes no tool calls. It also covers missing `call_id`, an unrelated item `id`, malformed output shapes, malformed message parts, partial text under an unknown status, valid completion, valid refusal, and a valid completed tool request.

The independent learner variation changes the incomplete reason to `content_filter`, changes the response id and partial text, and leaves a ready call-shaped item present. The answer is `other`, the text remains available, `rawStop` remains `content_filter`, and `toolCalls` remains empty. The causal reason is that the response is still incomplete and this focused contract establishes only `max_output_tokens` as a truncation mapping.
Recovery copies `adapter.starter.mjs` over `adapter.mjs`. The independent reference is in `adapter.reference.mjs`. The verifier imports neither the starter copy nor the reference.

activity.title: Repair and probe a final-response adapter
instructions: Run the verifier from the repository root and confirm the documented 16-pass, 1-failure starter result and exit code 1.
Inspect the fixture. Explain why `status: "incomplete"` prevents its function-call item from becoming executable even though the item has a valid `call_id`.
Repair only the incomplete-branch ordering in `adapter.mjs`. Do not edit the fixture, verifier, starter copy, or reference.
Run the verifier again and confirm 17 passes, 0 failures, and exit code 0.
Run `variation.mjs`. Explain why `content_filter` maps to `other`, retains partial text and `rawStop`, and exposes no tool calls.
Sketch equivalent state-first rules for Claude Messages and either Gemini surface using their native field names.
Optional live track: use project-approved credentials for one bounded, cancellable native request. Keep its evidence separate from the fixture result.
evidence: The repaired `adapter.mjs` with the verifier and fixture unchanged.
The exact repaired verifier output and exit code 0.
The exact variation output and exit code 0.
A causal explanation distinguishing incomplete, complete, refusal, tool request, and malformed results.
A provider-specific mapping sketch that does not invent a universal wire schema.
activity.reflectionPrompt: What downstream side effect could occur if an adapter exposed a call-shaped item before confirming that its final response was completed?

questions.prompt: A Claude response has stop_reason `max_tokens`. What should the adapter report?
questions.explanation: `max_tokens` indicates that generation reached a token limit, so the returned text may be incomplete.

questions.prompt: An OpenAI final response has status `incomplete`, reason `max_output_tokens`, partial text, and a valid-looking function call. What may this adapter expose?
choices: A completed answer and executable call
A truncated result with partial text and no executable calls
questions.explanation: Incomplete status takes precedence. Partial text is retained, but the call is not authorized.

questions.prompt: Why must a function-call item's ordinary `id` not be used when `call_id` is absent?
choices: Every item id is a secret
The fields identify different things, and this contract requires the actual call_id used for tool-result correlation
questions.explanation: Substituting an unrelated item identifier can break correlation or attach a tool result to the wrong protocol object.

questions.prompt: How should a final snapshot with status `queued` and a call-shaped item be classified by this lab adapter?
choices: Other, with no executable tool calls
questions.explanation: Queued is noncompleted. A final-response adapter must not release its call-shaped item for execution.

questions.prompt: What should happen when `output` or a message `content` value has a malformed shape?
choices: Execute any function call that can still be found
questions.explanation: The boundary parser validates arrays and records before traversal. Malformed input becomes `other`.

questions.prompt: What does Anthropic document about `strict` tools on its OpenAI SDK compatibility route?
choices: They are converted into Gemini tools
questions.explanation: Anthropic documents that the compatibility layer ignores the strict tool flag.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly separates fixture and integration testing?
choices: Fixture success proves current model availability
A fixture tests local deterministic parsing, while an authenticated integration test checks a configured live route
questions.explanation: The offline fixture cannot establish provider availability, account access, billing, or live model behavior.

questions.prompt: When may a mutation be retried safely?
choices: When the operation documents idempotency, the same key is reused, and the policy remains bounded
questions.explanation: Mutation retries need an operation-specific idempotency guarantee plus bounded attempts, budget, and cancellation.
